doc.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Herman Foster, the genius pianist
summary: Herman Foster needed no rehearsals and stole the show from Dave Brubeck in Belgium.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Herman Foster most of the time.
You linked up with him again for a long time in the ‘80s before you went back to the organ format.

They never said a thing about Herman, and Herman was a genius. Herman was a guy... Sometimes we’d play a year and never have a rehearsal. He knew everything. He was a genius. We played a concert once in Belgium. The guy had Dave Brubeck on there. I went and told the promoter, “You’d better let us play last, because if we play before Dave Brubeck, people are going to leave.” He said, “No-no-no, this is Dave Brubeck.” So Herman got to doing his stuff. Shee... Dave Brubeck came on, and everybody was outside trying to get Herman’s autograph.
